title: HTTP
description:
HTTP APIs written as curl commands: lists, wrapped lists, a redirect, a JSON POST, a
quoted argument and a login kept in a cookie file. Needs `make it-up` (port 18080).
See `:help dbdash-http`.

args.name: q
args.description: Sent URL-encoded by the quoting panel

show.title: A JSON list of objects: rows as they are
show.description:
`curl /items` GETs `http://127.0.0.1:18080/items`; a JSON list of objects is shown as
rows without a transform.

show.title: A wrapped list: query.transform takes it out
show.description:
`-G -d page=1` sends the data as URL parameters (`/wrapped?page=1`). The rows are
inside `data.items`: `query.transform` takes them out, and reads `response.status`.

show.title: A redirect (301) followed with -L
show.description:
`/old` answers 301 to `/items`; as with curl, `-L` follows it (`--max-redirs N`
limits how many). Without `-L` the 301 itself is the answer, shown as an error.

show.title: A POST with --json and a header
show.description:
`--json` sends a JSON body with its Content-Type and Accept (`-d` would send a form,
as curl does); `-H` adds a header.

show.title: An argument as one quoted word
show.description:
With `query.autoescape`, `{{ args.q }}` is written as a shell-quoted word, so a value
such as `it's a test` cannot break the command (`| shell_quote` does the same
without autoescape). `-G` moves the data, URL-encoded, to the URL: `?q=it%27s...`.

query.transform:
-- The first refresh logs in (the server sets a cookie, written to .cookies.txt);
-- later ones read it back and show what was sent.
if response.url:find("/login") then return { { cookie = "(logged in; refresh with r)" } } end
return rs

show.title: A login kept in a cookie file (-b / -c)
show.description:
As with curl: the first refresh logs in and `-c .cookies.txt` writes the cookie the
server set (next to this file); later refreshes read it with `-b .cookies.txt` (and
send `-b 'lang=zh'` too) to `/whoami`, which echoes them. Press `r`. A config that
writes a cookie file asks whether you trust it first.
